It depends on your resolution how much margin will appear on either side. There's a usable width (generally 1200 to 1600 pixels) and anything larger is actually worse user experience. Websites are designed to infinitely expand downward, so if you have more content to show, it can go lower down. If you try to utilize more horizontal space, you degrade the user experience, especially on larger resolutions. On my 1440p monitor, the content takes up about half the screen. If it took up the entire width it would be terrible. Moving my eyes and head around that much to view all the content would make me shrink the window size to compensate.

The current width (and responsiveness) is ideal and should not be changed.

I have a triple monitor setup with all three in portrait mode, and vastly prefer narrow/tall to wide/short. With the browser filling a single monitor, I zoom VoAt just enough to make the sidebar disappear into the menu at the top left and love the look and feel (it's identical to the smartphone layout but with smaller fonts). No margins, no empty space anywhere, and nothing unnecessary on the screen.

The current width (and responsiveness) is ideal and should not be changed.

The current width is far from ideal and should be changed.

unsafeWindow.toggleFullWidth = function()
{
 if( $('#FullWidth_css').length )
 $('#FullWidth_css').remove();
 else
 {
 var css = "\
 #header-account {\
 right: 2% !important;\
 }\
 \
 #header-banner, #container {\
 max-width: 100% !important;\
 }\
 .usertext {\
 max-width: 75% !important;\
 }\
 .commenttextarea {\
 max-width: 35% !important;\
 }";
 var style = document.createElement('style');
 style.type = 'text/css';
 style.id = 'FullWidth_css';
 if( style.styleSheet )
 style.styleSheet.cssText = css;
 else
 style.appendChild(document.createTextNode(css));
 document.body.appendChild(style);
 }
}

It is not wasted space. The container aims to displace the whitespace usually located in the middle of the page to the outsides. Removing the container would not yield more used space since comments would then need a limit on the characters-per-line so readability doesn't suffer (even Reddit does this). There are no compelling reasons to remove the container layout and so, therefore, there are no plans for it to be removed.

As for keeping the container layout and utilizing the wasted space more for widescreen users, maybe a multi-column post feed (like Google+) could be the solution.
